sections.h2: Where a Pitt County deed gets recorded
sections.html:
Deeds for Pitt County land are recorded at the Pitt County Register of Deeds, 100 E. 1st Street in Greenville. Weekday hours are 8:00 to 5:00, the phone is 252-902-1650 and the fax is 252-830-4132.

The same office keeps deeds, deeds of trust, easements, plats and the other land papers that make up the chain of title. For a seller, the office matters at one moment above all: the deed that moves the house to a buyer has to land in these books before it protects anyone.

sections.h2: Why filing order matters in a sale
sections.html:
The first paper on file wins. Under the state recording statute, an unfiled deed or option has no force against creditors with liens or buyers who paid value, and ranking among claims follows filing time.

Greenville is where that time stamp gets set, which is why every closing ends with a filing step. A signed deed left in a drawer protects nobody. If you hold an old deed from a family transfer that never reached the office, file it, or talk to an attorney, before you advertise the house.

The General Assembly sets the fees, and they are the same in every county.

Pitt County recording charges
FilingCharge
General instrument (deed, easement)$26 through page 15, then $4 per page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 with a 35-page allowance
Plat$21 per sheet
Non-standard document$25 extra
Certified copy$5 for page one, $2 per extra page
Mortgage releaseNo charge
PhotocopiesTypically $0.25 per page
UCC filing, 1 to 2 pages$38

The lender figure comes from G.S. 161-10. Call before sending a lender document so the check matches. The office accepts cash, check, money order and card.

The excise tax runs a dollar for every $500 of price, with a leftover part of $500 counting as a full one. It follows the sale price.

The seller carries the duty under the excise tax statute, and it has to be paid before the register will accept the deed. Pitt keeps half the money and the State receives the other half. Look for the line on your settlement statement.

Yes, Pitt County takes electronic filings through several vendors, and filers should call each one to compare prices. Four vendors are listed on the county FAQ, each with its own phone number.

Most sellers never touch this step, since the closing office sends the deed and the buyer's loan papers together. A family transfer with no lender is different: ask whoever prepared the deed whether they file electronically or in person, and who covers the vendor charge.

sections.h2: Watching for deed fraud and checking records
sections.html:
Pitt County has an alert sign-up that notifies owners whenever a filing matches their name or property. The county also runs an online search for recorded documents from September 1762 to the present, searchable by grantor, grantee, document type, book and page, or date range.

  • Search the grantor index for your name to see every recorded deed or lien tied to you.
  • Use book and page numbers from an old deed to pull the full document.
  • Use the Online Parcel Information System, run by Tax Administration and GIS, to view parcel boundaries, assessed values, tax districts and flood zones.
  • Older index books can be used on site at the Greenville office.

Do this before listing, especially with an inherited house. A loan that was never released, or a missing link in the ownership record, takes less effort to fix while no buyer is waiting.

sections.h2: Other papers in a Pitt County sale
sections.html:
Besides the deed, a closing can include a deed of trust for the buyer's loan, a recorded release of the seller's old loan, and sometimes a plat or easement. Each one is filed separately and priced under the fee list above.

  • Old loan: confirm the lender recorded a satisfaction.
  • New loan: the buyer's lender records its own deed of trust.
  • Seller financing: Chapter 47H calls for recording the contract within five business days.

The office also records agreements, assignments, assumed names, leases and subdivision maps.

sections.h2: Other services at the register's office
sections.html:
The office is more than a deed counter. It holds birth and death certificates for events in the county, issues marriage licenses, files notary commissions and gives the oath to every notary public. A veteran can file military discharge records here, and the charge for filing or copying them is waived.

It also takes Uniform Commercial Code financing statements on personal property, listed at $38 for one or two pages. The overlap that helps sellers is notary service. A $10 notarial act fee is tied to a filing, so someone who has not yet signed a deed can ask about doing it at the counter. Call 252-902-1650 first, and bring photo identification.

sections.h2: Old deeds and the chain of title
sections.html:
Pitt County was formed in 1760, and its oldest records include land grants, indentures and property agreements from the 1700s. Online search reaches back to September 1762, and index books for older records are kept on site. Look up the grantor or grantee in the alphabetical index, note the book and page, then pull the full document with that reference.

An old farm or family tract can have a chain of deeds that runs back generations. If a deed in that chain was never filed, or a name is spelled differently from one deed to the next, a buyer's title search will flag it. Start the search early, and keep every book and page number you find.

sections.h2: What a Pitt County seller should do before closing
sections.html:
Begin with a title check. Pull the deed that put the house in your name, confirm each old loan has a filed release, and ask the tax office what is owed.

Property tax lives in a different office. Under the collection statute, each bill falls due on September 1, and interest begins after January 5. Pitt County Tax Administration gives the balance on your parcel.

Repairs, tenants and estate delays do not block a quick sale to a direct cash buyer. The filing steps stay the same: the deed goes to Greenville.

sections.h2: Closing day paperwork in Pitt County
sections.html:
Once a contract is signed, the buyer's attorney searches the land records and requests your tax payoff. At closing you sign the deed, the stamp tax comes out of your proceeds, and the closing office sends the deed to the register in Greenville. The buyer's lender then files its deed of trust, and the release of your old loan is recorded if the lender has not already done so.

With a cash buyer there is no new deed of trust, so fewer papers go to the counter. Title work, the stamp tax and the tax payoff stay the same. Ask your attorney for the recorded copy showing the filing time, and keep it with your sale papers.

faqs.q: Where is the Pitt County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: At 100 E. 1st Street, Greenville, NC 27834. Weekdays only, 8:00 to 5:00, and the phone is 252-902-1650.

faqs.q: Who covers the deed stamp tax in a Pitt County sale?
faqs.a: Sellers do. The statute names the transferor, and the office takes the payment at the counter. Your settlement statement should show the line.

faqs.q: Is there a charge to file a mortgage release in Pitt County?
faqs.a: No. Satisfactions and cancellations are free. The lender files the release, so ask yours to do it.

faqs.q: Is there an online deed search for Pitt County?
faqs.a: Yes. Documents recorded from September 1762 forward can be searched online by name, type, book and page, or dates.

faqs.q: What is the base fee for a Pitt County deed?
faqs.a: $26 buys a general instrument of up to 15 pages, then each extra page adds $4. Plats are $21 a sheet. Get the final total for your own document by phone.
